primary_task: Refactor a monolithic Terraform configuration into a reusable module (variables, outputs, docs, tests) with a moved-block state migration plan.

requirements.name: read/write local Terraform source files
requirements.evidence: 'Existing Terraform configuration to refactor'; '`source_directory` | string | Yes | Path to existing Terraform configuration'
requirements.basis: tools: 'read' and 'write: create and overwrite files'.

requirements.name: terraform CLI (state list, show -json, plan)
requirements.evidence: 'Access to inspect current state via `terraform state list` / `terraform show -json` (for migration planning)'; the document gives a fallback: 'Fall back to the raw state (`terraform state pull` / `terraform.tfstate`) only when providers aren't available and `init` can't run'
requirements.basis: The binary is not stated to be on PyPI/npm/apt/GitHub releases; releases.hashicorp.com and registry.terraform.io are not among the open hosts ('other hosts are refused'). Would need to check an installable route.

requirements.name: cloud provider (AWS) credentials / remote state backend for state access and apply-mode tests
requirements.evidence: 'preserve_state | boolean | Yes'; 'integration_test.tftest.hcl  # Integration test (apply mode - creates real resources)'; 'terraform plan -out=migration.tfplan'
requirements.basis: lacks: 'accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services ... (cloud providers such as AWS, Azure and GCP ...)'.

requirements.name: skill terraform-test
requirements.basis: tools: 'skill: load an installed Claude Code skill, list and search skills and plugins'; whether terraform-test is installed is not stated.

notes: Reading taken: the core deliverable is the module code plus moved blocks, which the agent writes from the local .tf files; state inspection has an explicit raw-state fallback, so terraform is not hard. Other reading: if preserve_state=true makes live state access and 'No plan differences after refactoring' (a success-criteria checkbox) mandatory, then terraform plus AWS credentials are required and the verdict would be BLOCKED.
